SPR Hit Caller

Load Biacore curve exports, set the injection schedule, mark negatives and no-template controls. Every curve's response is compared with a cutoff of the negatives' mean + 3 SD.

Showing the example: runs 2-3, 3-2 and 4-2, named from the plate layouts, with the tnfr designs and GFP-10 as negatives. Each run is called on its most concentrated injection, found automatically.

Results table ↓
Step 1

Runs

One Biacore export per run (text with columns like Ch=1 Fc=2-1_Y). Each channel becomes a curve named run-Ch#: 2-3-Ch3 is channel 3 of run 2-3. The run name comes from the file name and can be edited.

or drop .txt / .csv exports here. Select many at once.
Step 2

Injection schedule

Fill in the four boxes to generate the table. For uneven schedules, edit a start or end directly in the table. Check the shaded windows in the curve viewer below.

InjectionStart (s)End (s)Label (optional)
Windows and artifact checks
 

Defaults: before = 10 s to 1 s before the injection starts; during = 5 s after it starts to 2 s before it ends; the SD multiplier is set in the Hit call panel at the top. A curve gets "No call" if a window touches a saturated stretch, has missing points, contains a jump bigger than the spike limit, or the response is far below the negatives.

Check

Curve viewer

Every curve on one plot. Hover to identify a curve; click it to highlight it here, in the dot plot and in the table.

Layout Zero at Time
Step 3

Curves and roles

Negative: should not bind; these set the cutoff. No template: cell-free reaction without DNA; their average response is subtracted from every other curve. Exclude: left out of everything.

CurveSample nameRole
Step 4

Results

Each dot is one curve's response for its called injection, after the no-template average is subtracted. The dashed line is the cutoff.
